title_en: Li Xianzhi v. Changchun Construction Engineering Group — dispute over defining property rights and returning property
ruling_gist_en: 1. Since an internal department of a legal person does not have legal person status and has no independent legal person property, its establishment is not premised on whether there is capital contribution.
keywords_en: Civil; Property rights dispute; Dispute over return of property; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Jilin Province; Natural person; Legal person; General Principles of the Civil Law; Legal nature of internal departments of a legal person; Relationship between investor's rights and legal person's property rights; Nature of a contract for contractual operation; Dismissal of claims; Internal departments of a legal person; Contractual operation; Investment as capital contribution; Settlement of claims and debts
full_text_en:
SELECTED ADJUDICATORY DOCUMENTS

Li Xianzhi v. Changchun Construction Engineering Group — Dispute over Definition of Property Rights and Return of Property

【RULING SUMMARY】

1. An internal department of a legal person, lacking independent legal personality and independent法人 property, does not require the premise of property contribution for its establishment.

2. The nature of the operational mode adopted by an internal department of a legal person after its establishment, or whether others have contributed assets to it, cannot change its legal attribute as an internal department of a legal person.

3. After a contributor makes a capital contribution to a legal person, he may only claim corresponding equity rights and interests in respect of the shares he holds, and his contribution forms an indivisible part of the legal person's property.

CIVIL JUDGMENT OF THE SUPREME PEOPLE'S COURT

(2004) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 190

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Li Ming, male, Han ethnicity, born August 27, 1971, domiciled at: No. 6-14, Shui Lu, Chaoyang District, Changchun City, Jilin Province. ID number: 220104197108270357.

Agent ad litem: Li Jianhua, lawyer of Jilin Tiandize Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance): Changchun Construction Engineering Group Corporation. Domicile: Nanguan District, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal representative: Wang Zheng, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Jianxin, employee of the company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Qi, lawyer of Jilin Jingcheng Law Firm.

The former appellant Li Xianzhi and Changchun Construction Engineering Group Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the Construction Engineering Group), in a case against the respondent Changchun First Construction Engineering Company (hereinafter referred to as the First Construction Company) concerning a dispute over definition of property rights and return of property, once dissatisfied with the civil judgment (1998) Ji Jing Chu Zi No. 61 of the Jilin High People's Court in 2001, filed an appeal to this Court. This Court, by civil ruling (2001) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 69 dated October 25, 2001, remanded the case to the Jilin High People's Court for retrial. After retrial, the Jilin High People's Court rendered civil judgment (2002) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 12 on July 30, 2004. The appellant Li Ming (successor of the former appellant Li Xianzhi, who died of illness on April 9, 2004), dissatisfied with the said civil judgment of the Jilin High People's Court, filed an appeal to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of presiding judge Wu Qingbao, acting judges Gong Bangyou and Liu Min to conduct the trial. Court clerk Pan Yongfeng served as the recordkeeper. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found: At the end of 1985, after negotiation between Li Xianzhi and the First Construction Company, an independent legal person subordinate to the Construction Engineering Group, Li Xianzhi brought his own assets valued at over RMB 120,000 into the First Construction Company to establish the Fifth Engineering Department of the First Construction Company (hereinafter referred to as the First Construction Fifth Department). Li Xianzhi served as the director of the department, and the First Construction Company assigned deputy directors, financial personnel, and others to participate in management. At the same time, the First Construction Fifth Department arranged employment for 200 unemployed youths of the First Construction Company and paid management fees.

On August 1, 1988, Li Xianzhi and Luo Futing, the person in charge of the First Construction Company, entered into a contract (hereinafter referred to as the 1988 contract), which stated: In order to deepen enterprise reform, enhance enterprise vitality, mobilize the enthusiasm of operators through multiple channels, and improve enterprise economic efficiency, the manager of the First Construction Company signed a contract management agreement with Li Xianzhi, director of the First Construction Fifth Department. The annual contract management agreement signed by the First Construction Company with the First Construction Fifth Department was valid, and both parties must seriously implement it. In 1987, Comrade Li Xianzhi's investment of fixed assets in the company amounted to RMB 125,209, with dividends (annual interest rate) at 15%. For those who invested in shares, the First Construction Company would distribute dividends based on the realization of cost reduction targets (planned RMB 295,000), with a 40-60 split on the excess portion (60% to the company, 40% to the individual). The First Construction Company would distribute dividends before tax, and both investing parties must pay taxes according to the tax rates stipulated by higher authorities (individual income adjustment tax paid on behalf of the unit by the company). In case of conflict with higher authorities' regulations, the latter shall prevail. Luo Futing and Li Xianzhi signed the contract on behalf of both parties.

In 1992, Li Xianzhi resigned as director of the First Construction Fifth Department and left the First Construction Company.

In 1994, in accordance with the spirit of Changchun Municipal People's Government Letter (1994) No. 12 approving the conversion of the Changchun Construction Engineering Administration Bureau into an economic entity, the First Construction Company was restructured into the First Construction Company of the Construction Engineering Group (hereinafter referred to as the Construction Engineering Group First Construction Company), which did not have independent legal personality, and its creditor's rights and debts were assumed by the Construction Engineering Group.

On March 1, 1995, the Construction Engineering Group First Construction Company and Li Xianzhi settled their mutual creditor's rights and debts. The "Settlement List of Mutual Creditor's Rights and Debts of Construction Construction Units" (hereinafter referred to as the "1995 Settlement List") recorded: The First Construction Company was owed three sums by Li Xianzhi: RMB 170,000 for the transfer of the prefabrication plant on September 29, 1993; RMB 68,776.81 for the transfer of film-laying machines and other items on September 30; and RMB 293.88 for material payments and material tool rental fees on October 31. Li Xianzhi was owed eight sums by the First Construction Company: RMB 49,618.60 for transferred panels and X (difficult to identify) on July 31, 1993; RMB 338,240 for transferred current accounts on April 10; RMB 61,760 for transferred coal payments on June 30; RMB 100,000 for transferred loans; RMB 19,000 for brick payments to the 228 Factory on November 30; RMB 49,500 for cement payments in December; plus RMB 125,209 in pooled funds and RMB 18,000 in interest on pooled funds. After offsetting the amounts payable by both parties, the settlement result was that Li Xianzhi still owed the First Construction Company RMB 107,743.09. The Construction Engineering Group First Construction Company and Li Xianzhi respectively affixed their seals and signed the "1995 Settlement List". On April 9 of the same year, regarding the debt of RMB 107,743.09 still owed after the above liquidation, Li Xianzhi, in the name of another enterprise he operated, Changchun Zhixin Building Materials Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhixin Company), entered into an "Agreement on Repayment of Debts on Behalf" with the Construction Engineering Group, stipulating that Zhixin Company would use the RMB 107,743.09 it owed to the Construction Engineering Group to repay the following debts on behalf of the Construction Engineering Group: 1. Repay RMB 49,828.62 in material payments to Beijing Housing Management First Company; 2. Repay RMB 57,660 in coal payments to Changchun Commodity Inspection Bureau. The total of the above two items was RMB 107,488.62, and the remaining RMB 254.47 was to be transferred by Zhixin Company to the Construction Engineering Group's account via bank within 15 days after the agreement took effect. On November 30 of the same year, the accounting voucher No. 444 of the Construction Engineering Group First Construction Company showed that Zhixin Company paid RMB 57,660 in coal payments to Changchun Commodity Inspection Bureau and RMB 49,828.62 to Beijing Housing Management First Company.

During the first-instance trial, Li Xianzhi admitted that from 1987 to 1992 he actually received a total of six payments of dividends and bonuses from the First Construction Company, totaling RMB 111,837.11. These were: RMB 24,000 in bonus payment on August 6, 1987; RMB 13,632 in "individual share interest" and RMB 21,423.76 in "bonuses" on December 31, 1987; RMB 24,000 on February 2, 1989; RMB 18,781.35 in "dividends" on February 2, 1989; and RMB 10,000 in "dividends" on November 18, 1992. Li Xianzhi did not acknowledge other payment vouchers and accounting vouchers for dividend payments to him produced by the Construction Engineering Group.

It was also found that the "Request Report of the First Construction Company on the Establishment of the First Construction Fifth Department" submitted by the First Construction Company to the Changchun Construction Engineering General Company in 1985 stated that, in order to meet the needs of economic system reform, further enhance enterprise vitality, and improve economic efficiency, the company decided to establish the First Construction Fifth Department. The "Interim Measures for the Implementation of Independent Accounting and Self-Financing Management Contract of the First Construction Fifth Department" attached to the report defined the operational policy of the First Construction Fifth Department as: "within a state-owned enterprise, implement collective operation, independent accounting, payment of taxes and profits, self-financing, distribution according to work, and democratic management."

On February 2, 1988, the First Construction Company issued Document Chang Yi Jian Zi (88) No. 8, "Notice on Dismissing Fifty Administrative Mid-Level Cadres Including Zhang Wenshi," stating: "All Engineering Departments and Sections: The company's three-year manager responsibility system from January 1985 to December 1987 has expired. According to the opinion of Manager Luo Futing and the decision of the manager meeting, the previous selection and appointment of administrative mid-level cadres is terminated... Comrade Li Xianzhi is removed from the position of director of the First Construction Fifth Department..." On February 6 of the same year, the First Construction Company issued another "Notice on Selecting and Appointing Fifty-Nine Comrades Including Zhang Wenshi as Administrative Mid-Level Cadres," which decided, "according to the nomination of Manager Luo Futing and the decision of the manager meeting, after consulting the Standing Committee," to select and appoint "Comrade Li Xianzhi as director of the First Construction Fifth Department."

A copy of a contract provided by Li Xianzhi, allegedly signed on January 1, 1986, between him and Luo Futing, the person in charge of the First Construction Company, stated that in order to deepen enterprise reform, enhance enterprise vitality, mobilize the enthusiasm of operators through multiple channels, and improve enterprise economic efficiency, the manager of the First Construction Company and Li Xianzhi jointly invested to establish the First Construction Fifth Department. Comrade Li Xianzhi's investment of fixed assets in 1986 amounted to RMB 125,209 as share capital, with dividends (annual interest rate) at 15%. The company's investment amounted to RMB 880,000. For the excess portion, there would be a 40-60 split (60% to the company, 40% to the individual), etc. Li Xianzhi could not produce the original contract, and the Construction Engineering Group did not acknowledge it.

The "Audit Appraisal Report" (1999) No. 794, commissioned by the court of first instance and prepared by Jilin Zhenhua Accounting Firm (hereinafter referred to as the "794 Audit Report"), stated that the audit results were based on part of the account books and accounting voucher materials provided by the First Construction Company and were not subject to comprehensive verification. The First Construction Fifth Department's profit from 1986 to 1992 was RMB 3,721,452.64, and regardless of profit or loss in each year, it was remitted to the First Construction Company through the credit side of "Internal Current Accounts." As of the end of 1992, the First Construction Company's "Fixed Fund - Funds Allocated from Higher Authorities" account had a remaining balance of RMB 1,575,374.23. From 1986 to 1992, the cumulative book input into "Fixed Fund - Funds Allocated from Higher Authorities" was RMB 1,971,593.22, of which RMB 778,948 had original vouchers (except for the enterprise self-raised RMB 125,209, the company invested equipment in the First Construction Fifth Department), and RMB 1,192,645.22 had no original vouchers. Among these, Voucher No. 83 in April 1987 recorded the enterprise self-raised RMB 125,209 as equipment investment under the "Fixed Fund - Enterprise Self-Raised" account, and Voucher No. 246 on December 31, 1988, allocated RMB 108,904.78 (verified) into "Fixed Fund - Funds Allocated from Higher Authorities," Voucher No. 506 on December 31, 1988, transferred RMB 13,520 (verified) into "Fixed Fund - Funds Allocated from Higher Authorities," and Voucher No. 187 on December 30, 1987, recorded the First Construction Company's payment of interest of RMB 13,632 on Li Xianzhi's share investment. From 1986 to 1992, the First Construction Fifth Department remitted RMB 4,823,376.54 to the company through "Internal Current Accounts," including RMB 1,984,647.80 in management fees, RMB 2,158,416.68 in special funds, RMB 180,305.30 in dedicated funds, and RMB 200,006.76 in depreciation funds. As of the end of 1992, the credit balance of "Internal Current Accounts - Company Finance Section" was RMB 6,119,389.16. Subsequently, Jilin Zhenhua Accounting Firm made a supplementary explanation to the above audit report, stating that when the First Construction Company was established, i.e., in 1987, a total of RMB 332,798.70 was invested, of which RMB 207,589.70 was allocated by the First Construction Company (verified through internal allocation of equipment, etc., at RMB 89,039.70, unverified at RMB 118,550), and the enterprise self-raised RMB 125,209 was recorded on a single sheet of paper, and the authenticity could not be confirmed based on existing materials. Li Xianzhi objected to the above "794 Audit Report" on the grounds that the 1996 account books of the First Construction Fifth Department were missing, and the Construction Engineering Group acknowledged that the 1996 account books were not audited, stating at trial that the relevant account books could no longer be found due to the restructuring of the First Construction Company.

During the retrial of this case, the plaintiff Li Xianzhi died on April 9, 2004. Li Ming is Li Xianzhi's sole legal successor and stated that he did not waive the right to litigate in this case. The court of first instance lawfully changed the plaintiff in this case to Li Ming.

On December 23, 1997, Li Xianzhi filed a lawsuit with the Changchun Intermediate People's Court, claiming that the First Construction Fifth Department was a private enterprise established with his personal investment and that all property rights in it belonged to him personally. He requested a judgment ordering the Construction Engineering Group to return all equipment, working capital, and fixed assets of the First Construction Fifth Department (amounting to approximately RMB 6 million) and that the Construction Engineering Group bear the litigation costs, etc. Later, Li Xianzhi added claims requesting a judgment ordering the Construction Engineering Group to return RMB 3 million in remitted profits and to pay RMB 4.8 million for 17,000 square meters of land and housing costs. Because the subject matter of Li Xianzhi's claims exceeded the acceptance standard of the Changchun Intermediate People's Court, on May 22, 1998, the Jilin High People's Court instructed the Changchun Intermediate People's Court to transfer the case to the Jilin High People's Court for trial. On June 18, 1998, Li Xianzhi filed a new complaint with the Jilin High People's Court against the First Construction Company and the Construction Engineering Group as defendants, seeking confirmation that the First Construction Company and the Construction Engineering Group had infringed upon his rights, that all property of the First Construction Fifth Department belonged to him, and a judgment ordering the First Construction Company and the Construction Engineering Group to return property worth no less than RMB 10 million (specific amount to be determined based on audit and appraisal conclusions) plus interest, and that the two defendants bear the case acceptance fees.

The court of first instance held that: First, regarding whether Li Xianzhi's additional claims of over RMB 10 million in the remanded retrial exceeded the statute of limitations. In Li Xianzhi's initial complaint to the court in 1998, the claim was "order the defendant Construction Engineering Group to return to the plaintiff Li Xianzhi property worth no less than RMB 10 million," which was ambiguous as to the specific amount claimed. The first-instance collegial panel did not require Li Xianzhi to clarify the claim. In this retrial, Li Xianzhi reorganized the complaint, specifying a total claim for return of property of RMB 20,017,853.88, which was a concretization of the claim, not the addition of a new claim. Therefore, the court did not accept the Construction Engineering Group's defense that the part of Li Xianzhi's additional claims exceeded the statute of limitations.

Second, regarding the nature of the First Construction Fifth Department and the relationship between Li Xianzhi and the First Construction Fifth Department. First, the First Construction Fifth Department was established at the end of 1985. It was an internal independent accounting unit of the enterprise, established by the First Construction Company based on enterprise development needs, approved by the Construction Engineering Bureau, and set up in accordance with the procedures for establishing a state-owned enterprise. At the time of establishment, the nature of the First Construction Fifth Department was that of a branch of a state-owned enterprise. After its establishment, the First Construction Company appointed Li Xianzhi as the head of the First Construction Fifth Department and assigned some of its own employees as other principal management personnel and technical persons in charge to jointly operate the First Construction Fifth Department. The First Construction Fifth Department was responsible for the work and remuneration of the employees assigned by the First Construction Company. As for the composition of the property of the First Construction Fifth Department, at the time of its establishment, Li Xianzhi brought construction equipment worth over RMB 120,000 and undertook projects externally in the name of the First Construction Fifth Department. During this period, the First Construction Company made no financial investment in the First Construction Fifth Department.

From the 1988 contract, it can be determined that, after negotiation between the parties, the construction equipment brought by Li Xianzhi was valued at RMB 125,209 and treated as Li Xianzhi's investment capital contribution added to the total property of the First Construction Fifth Department. Therefore, regardless of how Li Xianzhi's capital contribution of RMB 125,209 is characterized, objectively, the total property of the First Construction Fifth Department included a certain investment from Li Xianzhi. Although Li Xianzhi's witnesses provided counter-evidence against the First Construction Company's investment of RMB 1,846,383.62 in the First Construction Fifth Department as recorded in the "794 Audit Report," so the audit report cannot be directly relied upon to conclude that the First Construction Company made an investment in the First Construction Fifth Department, Wang Jingshan, former deputy director of the First Construction Fifth Department, also testified that when the Second Engineering Department of the First Construction Company was abolished, the First Construction Company allocated some personnel and tools to the First Construction Fifth Department. Therefore, Li Xianzhi's assertion that the First Construction Company made no financial or in-kind investment in the First Construction Fifth Department is also incorrect, although the specific amount cannot be determined.

Secondly, Branch 5 was a department under the Municipal No.1 Construction Company and did not have the status of a legal person. Any projects it undertook externally were contracted under the name of the Municipal No.1 Construction Company by entering into construction project contracts. Although the actual construction was carried out by Branch 5, the contractual liability should be independently borne by the Municipal No.1 Construction Company, the legal person to which Branch 5 belonged. At the same time, the fee rates for Branch 5's construction were determined based on the qualification standards of its legal person, the Municipal No.1 Construction Company. This was significantly different from the economic benefits Li Xianzhi would have obtained if he had personally entered into contracts with construction units. Although the Municipal No.1 Construction Company did not appraise or value its qualification grade when it signed the contract with Li Xianzhi in 1988, a portion of the profits generated by Branch 5 from its establishment until 1992 necessarily derived from the Municipal No.1 Construction Company's first-grade qualification and its commercial reputation in Changchun at that time. In other words, Branch 5 did not achieve its later growth and expansion solely through Li Xianzhi's personal capital and physical asset contributions. The intangible assets owned by the Municipal No.1 Construction Company at the time were an essential component for Branch 5's production and operations. Thirdly, Branch 5 borrowed RMB 4.5 million from banks during its operation. Regardless of whether the loan contract was signed with the financial institution in the name of Branch 5 or the Municipal No.1 Construction Company at the time of borrowing, since Branch 5 did not have the status of a legal person, the liable party for such loan contract was necessarily the Municipal No.1 Construction Company, not Branch 5. The reason the financial institution agreed to lend RMB 4.5 million for Branch 5's use was that Branch 5 was the No.1 Branch of the Municipal No.1 Construction Company, not Li Xianzhi's personal branch. If the loan was not repaid upon maturity, the Municipal No.1 Construction Company was the natural liable party. In summary, the Municipal No.1 Construction Company made physical asset investments in Branch 5; its qualification and commercial reputation provided the necessary prerequisites for Branch 5's lawful operations, and also brought Branch 5 higher economic benefits and liability protection. According to the provisions of Article 8, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the "Interim Measures for the Definition of State-owned Property Rights and Handling of Property Rights Disputes" of the State-owned Assets Administration Bureau, which stipulates: "The after-tax profits formed by a wholly people-owned enterprise using state capital funds and funds borrowed in the course of operation, which are approved by the state to be retained by the enterprise as additional investment, as well as the surplus reserve fund, public welfare fund, and undistributed profits withdrawn from after-tax profits, shall be defined as state-owned assets;" and Item 5 of the same Article, which stipulates: "The employee welfare fund and employee bonus fund withdrawn from retained profits by a wholly people-owned enterprise, and the collective welfare facilities constructed using the public welfare fund after the implementation of the 'Two Rules' (the Financial Rules and Accounting Rules for Enterprises), which correspondingly increase the owner's equity, shall be defined as state-owned assets;" and the provisions of Document No. 10 [1998] issued by the Changchun Municipal Committee of the Communist Party of China, "Several Provisions on Accelerating the Reform of Small Enterprises," which stipulates: "Enterprise property rights shall be defined in accordance with the principle of 'who invests, who owns, who benefits': assets invested by the state and the accumulated assets formed therefrom over the years shall belong to the state; assets invested by individual employees and the accumulated assets formed over the years, if the investor can be proven, the property rights shall belong to the individual workers... The assets formed by preferential policies enjoyed in accordance with state laws, regulations, and policies, including pre-tax loan repayment and various tax reductions and exemptions, shall belong to the enterprise," Li Xianzhi's claim that the property and income of Branch 5 were owned by him personally cannot be sustained. The court did not support Li Xianzhi's request for a judgment ordering the Construction Engineering Group to return all the property. During the litigation, Li Xianzhi and his agent ad litem emphasized that Li Xianzhi and the Municipal No.1 Construction Company had signed a joint venture contract on January 1, 1986, but they failed to produce the original contract to the court. Although his witness, Wang Jingshan, the former deputy director of Branch 5, testified that he had seen this contract, a contract that determines whether a legal relationship exists between the parties, without the original and when the other party does not recognize it, cannot be determined to exist merely based on one person's testimony. Therefore, in accordance with Article 69 of the "Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," which provides that "copies or reproductions that cannot be verified against the original or the original object shall not be used alone as the basis for determining the facts of a case," the court refused to recognize the authenticity of the joint venture contract claimed by Li Xianzhi to have been signed on January 1, 1986. From the evidence jointly submitted by Li Xianzhi and the Construction Engineering Group to the court during the trial, including the "Interim Measures for Implementing Independent Accounting and Self-financing Business Contracting for Branch 5" and the Municipal No.1 Construction Company's notices No. 8 [1988] titled "Notice on the Removal of 50 Mid-level Administrative Cadres including Zhang Wenshi" and "Notice on the Selection and Appointment of 59 Comrades including Zhang Wenshi as Mid-level Administrative Cadres," it can be concluded that at the time of establishing Branch 5, the Municipal No.1 Construction Company set up and managed Branch 5 in accordance with the enterprise's internal contracting method. Furthermore, the 1988 contract further clarified that prior to August 1, 1988, the legal relationship between the two parties was enterprise contracting, and it was determined that the contracting relationship would continue. As for the specific rights and obligations under the previous contract, they cannot be known in detail because the parties to the case did not submit or could not submit the original contract. Article 2 of that contract set the price of fixed assets brought by Li Xianzhi into Branch 5 at RMB 125,209. The nature of this, in terms of wording, was an investment in shares, but in substance it was a loan. Because once an investor invests in shares, he should enjoy shareholder rights based on that capital as his investment proportion in the company's equity, and bear limited liability within the scope of the capital contributed. There is no fixed dividend, nor is there a final withdrawal of capital without liquidation. During the performance of this contract, Li Xianzhi indeed received from the Municipal No.1 Construction Company a fixed interest of 15% on the principal of RMB 125,209, and in the "Settlement List of Debts and Credits Between the Construction Unit and the Contractor" (hereinafter referred to as the "1995 Settlement List"), signed by Li Xianzhi and stamped with the Municipal No.1 Construction Company's seal on March 1, 1995, it is reflected that Li Xianzhi had fully recovered that capital. Therefore, the nature of this amount should be an ordinary loan or enterprise fundraising. Article 3 of that contract relatively clearly stipulated the rights and obligations of Li Xianzhi under the contract, i.e., after Li Xianzhi completed an annual construction profit of RMB 295,000, the excess part would be divided between Li Xianzhi and the Municipal No.1 Construction Company at 40% and 60% respectively, thereby further clarifying the contractual management relationship between Li Xianzhi and the Municipal No.1 Construction Company. This contract was signed by Li Xianzhi and the Municipal No.1 Construction Company, reflecting the true intent of both parties, and does not violate the relevant provisions of China's current laws and regulations, so the contract is legal and valid. In summary, from its inception, Branch 5, as an internal institution of the wholly people-owned enterprise the Municipal No.1 Construction Company, naturally had a wholly people-owned nature. It was entirely established and managed according to the internal mechanism of the Municipal No.1 Construction Company. Only in terms of enterprise assets did it complete its initial capital accumulation by borrowing machinery and equipment from Li Xianzhi, and then it was contracted out to Li Xianzhi under the enterprise contracting mechanism. A clear legal relationship of contractual management of an enterprise was formed between Li Xianzhi and the Municipal No.1 Construction Company. Since the RMB 125,209 mentioned in the contract as invested by Li Xianzhi was a loan, after Li Xianzhi contributed it to Branch 5, the ownership of the physical assets represented by that portion of funds transferred to the Municipal No.1 Construction Company. Therefore, Branch 5 was able to include it in its financial accounts. From that point on, Li Xianzhi no longer had any right to possess, use, benefit from, or dispose of those assets. What Li Xianzhi enjoyed was only a creditor's right arising from the transfer of this property right, i.e., the right to demand the Municipal No.1 Construction Company pay the principal of RMB 125,209 and related interest. Consequently, the income, profits, etc., generated from the physical assets corresponding to the RMB 125,209 in the course of operations should all belong to their new owner, the Municipal No.1 Construction Company, and Li Xianzhi has no right to claim them.

Third, regarding whether a creditor-debtor relationship existed between the Municipal No.1 Construction Company and Li Xianzhi, and the specific amount thereof. In this case, the legal relationship between Li Xianzhi and the Municipal No.1 Construction Company was a dual one of contractual management and loan. Whether Li Xianzhi had a creditor's right against the Municipal No.1 Construction Company should be analyzed and determined based on whether Li Xianzhi had fulfilled the profit targets under the contract management and whether the loan relationship had been terminated. According to the 1988 contract, the original intent was that Li Xianzhi must annually achieve a cost reduction amount of RMB 295,000 before he could receive 40% of the profits. According to the written explanation provided by the Provincial Construction Department, the term "cost reduction amount" refers to the difference between the project profit and the statutory profit (planned profit). Jilin Zhongxin Accounting Firm Co., Ltd. explained the term "construction profit" to the Economic Judicial Appraisal Center of the court on April 19, 2001: "construction profit" is the "cost reduction amount." From the "Profit Payment Table" in the "Audit Report No. 794," it can be seen that during the five years from 1988 to 1992, Li Xianzhi only achieved a construction profit of RMB 304,917.44 in 1988, exceeding the target of RMB 295,000. In other years, he failed to meet the target. Based on this, it can be calculated that Li Xianzhi was only entitled to dividends in 1988: (304,917.44 - 295,000) x 40% = RMB 3,966.98. Li Xianzhi lent RMB 125,209 to the Municipal No.1 Construction Company. As agreed by both parties, the Municipal No.1 Construction Company was to pay Li Xianzhi 15% interest annually, i.e., Li Xianzhi was entitled to interest from 1988 to 1992: 125,209 x 15% x 5 = RMB 93,906.75. During the trial, Li Xianzhi acknowledged that he had already received a total of RMB 111,837.11 in dividends and interest from the Municipal No.1 Construction Company. Although Li Xianzhi challenged the authenticity of the "1995 Settlement List" submitted by the Construction Engineering Group and requested a handwriting expert examination of his signature on that list, he failed to pay the relevant expert examination fees within the time limit set by the court. Therefore, the court did not support his claim that the signature on the list was not his own. In terms of form, the "1995 Settlement List" appears to be a summary and settlement of numerous prior financial transactions between the two parties. In terms of substance, it includes the final treatment of the RMB 125,209 in assets initially lent by Li Xianzhi to the Municipal No.1 Construction Company and the related interest rights. It reflects a comprehensive clearing of accounts regarding the contractual management relationship, loan relationship, and other business dealings that had formed over many years between the two parties. It is the settlement of all debts and credits arising from all economic transactions between the two parties prior to 1995. The conclusion of the "1995 Settlement List" was that Li Xianzhi still owed the Municipal No.1 Construction Company RMB 107,743.09. Subsequently, Li Xianzhi and the Municipal No.1 Construction Company entered into a new repayment agreement regarding this debt, which was actually performed. This further objectively demonstrates that the two parties had fully settled all economic relations prior to 1995. Otherwise, Li Xianzhi would not have acknowledged owing the Municipal No.1 Construction Company RMB 107,743.09. He should have either asserted any remaining rights he had, offsetting the debt, or noted the reservation of such rights on the list. However, Li Xianzhi neither asserted such rights nor noted any reservation. The fact that Li Xianzhi entered into an agreement with the Construction Engineering Group to repay the debt on his behalf and actually performed the repayment obligation further indicates that the "1995 Settlement List" was the final conclusion of all debts and credits between the two parties. Therefore, the court did not support Li Xianzhi's aforementioned claims. The creditor's rights arising from various economic transactions between Li Xianzhi and the Municipal No.1 Construction Company prior to 1995 no longer existed.

Regarding the issue of the two plots of land claimed by Li Xianzhi. The first plot of land claimed by Li Xianzhi was purchased when Li Xianzhi was affiliated with the Labor Service Company of the Municipal No.1 Construction Company (a collectively-owned enterprise, hereinafter referred to as the "Labor Service Company of No.1 Construction") before the establishment of Branch 5, and the purchase was made in the name of the Labor Service Company of No.1 Construction. Li Xianzhi claimed he paid RMB 300,000. However, during the trial of this case, Li Xianzhi never produced the relevant contract and receipt for the purchase of that land. Moreover, the Labor Service Company of No.1 Construction is an independent legal person. If Li Xianzhi truly enjoyed the land use right, he should assert his rights separately against the Labor Service Company of No.1 Construction. In this case, because he failed to submit relevant evidence, the court could not find these facts and consequently could not protect his related claims. The second plot of land claimed by Li Xianzhi was leased by Branch 5 from the 16th Army Communication Regiment in 1988, during the period when Li Xianzhi was contracting Branch 5, for a term of 15 years. During the lease term, Branch 5 constructed some factories on that land. When Branch 5 was dissolved, the land and the buildings on it were taken back by the Municipal No.1 Construction Company. Subsequently, Li Xianzhi, in the name of Zhixin Company, repurchased them from the Municipal No.1 Construction Company on April 2, 1993, for RMB 1.7 million, and also paid RMB 150,000 to the military unit. Therefore, this land was leased by Branch 5 from the military unit during its production and operations. Branch 5 only enjoyed the leasehold right to the land, and that right, due to the nature of Branch 5 as an enterprise, naturally belonged to the Municipal No.1 Construction Company. The right to dispose of the factories built during the lease term should also belong to the Municipal No.1 Construction Company during the lease period. Li Xianzhi, as the person in charge of Branch 5, had no right to assert claims over such property rights. Therefore, based on the existing evidence in this case and the relevant provisions of China's current laws, it is difficult to conclude that the investment, establishment, operation, and development of Branch 5 were all accomplished by Li Xianzhi personally, and it is impossible to define the economic benefits created by Branch 5 as Li Xianzhi's personal property. Li Xianzhi's request for the Construction Engineering Group to return a total of RMB 20,017,853.88 plus interest lacks factual and legal basis. In accordance with Article 64, Paragraph 1 of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," which provides that "a party has the responsibility to provide evidence for its own claims," and the provisions of Article 69 of the "Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," and Article 8, Paragraph 1, Items 2 and 5 of the "Interim Measures for the Definition of State-owned Property Rights and Handling of Property Rights Disputes" of the State-owned Assets Administration Bureau, the court rendered a judgment dismissing Li Ming's claims. The case acceptance fee of RMB 110,609 was to be borne by Li Ming. The audit and appraisal fee of RMB 80,000 prepaid by Li Xianzhi was to be borne by Li Ming. The appeal fee for the Supreme People's Court's case No. (2001) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 69 was to be borne by Li Ming.

Li Ming, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Jilin Province High People's Court, appealed to this Court, arguing that Branch 5 was established solely with Li Xianzhi's capital, and the Municipal No.1 Construction Company made no capital contribution. Therefore, the property of Branch 5 and its accumulated and appreciated property should all belong to Li Xianzhi personally. The original judgment erred by denying Li Xianzhi's ownership of all the property of Branch 5 on the ground that Branch 5 was a branch of a wholly people-owned enterprise. Li Xianzhi argued that the relationship between Li Xianzhi and the Municipal No.1 Construction Company was not one of contractual management and loan, but rather that Li Xianzhi, based on his sole capital contribution, formed an investment relationship in shares with Branch 5, and that Branch 5, which he established with his capital, formed an affiliated operation relationship with the Municipal No.1 Construction Company. The several transactions listed in the "1995 Settlement List" all occurred in 1993 and should not be considered a settlement of all debts and credits between the parties over several years. The settlement was merely a settlement between the Construction Engineering Group and Zhixin Company regarding the transfer of the prefabrication plant and its accessories, and should not be used to conclude that all creditor's rights arising from various economic transactions between Li Xianzhi and the Municipal No.1 Construction Company prior to 1995 no longer existed. Li Xianzhi claimed he had lawful use rights to the two plots of land in question. He argued that the "Audit Report No. 794" was prepared based on some of the account books and accounting vouchers provided by Branch 5, but 11 account books from 1986 were missing, making the report incomplete and unreliable as a basis for judgment. Li Xianzhi argued that the original court erred in finding facts and applying the law. He requested the court of second instance to reverse the original judgment, confirm that the appellant was entitled to ownership of all the property and its income formed based on his investment in Branch 5, order the Construction Engineering Group to return a total of RMB 20,017,853.88 plus interest to Li Ming, and have the case acceptance fee and audit and appraisal fees borne by the Construction Engineering Group.

The appellee, the Construction Engineering Group, responded in defense, arguing that Branch 5 was established as an internal independent accounting unit within the enterprise, approved by the Construction Engineering Bureau in accordance with the procedures for establishing wholly people-owned enterprises. The "Audit Report No. 794" confirmed that the Municipal No.1 Construction Company had invested a total of RMB 1,846,383.62 in Branch 5 from 1987 to 1992, and during its operation, Branch 5 also borrowed RMB 4.5 million from banks. Therefore, the assets formed on this basis should be defined as state-owned assets. Branch 5's operations in the construction market were all carried out relying on the commercial reputation and first-grade qualification of the Municipal No.1 Construction Company. Without these, it would not have been able to secure projects and obtain first-grade fee rates. Moreover, as a wholly people-owned enterprise, Branch 5 enjoyed many preferential policies at that time, so the profits thus generated also belonged to the Municipal No.1 Construction Company. Although Li Xianzhi's investment of RMB 125,209 was described in words as an investment in shares, its substance was a fundraising-type loan. Li Xianzhi thus received the agreed 15% interest, and that amount had already been returned. Therefore, all the property of Branch 5 should be defined as state-owned assets, not personal property of Li Xianzhi. From 1985 to 1992, Li Xianzhi was a mid-level cadre appointed by the Municipal No.1 Construction Company, responsible for the management and operation of Branch 5. According to the 1988 contract, Li Xianzhi and Branch 5 were in a contractual management relationship, and the RMB 125,209 he contributed should be considered a loan. The rights Li Xianzhi could claim were his share of profits after meeting the contract targets and the principal and interest of the RMB 125,209 loan. His claim that Branch 5 belonged to him had no basis. The debts and credits between Branch 5 and Li Xianzhi had been settled through the "1995 Settlement List." That list included the treatment of the principal of the RMB 125,209 contributed by Li Xianzhi to Branch 5 and the payment of unsettled interest. It had the characteristics of a comprehensive settlement of numerous prior financial transactions between the two parties. According to this settlement, Branch 5 did not owe any money to Li Xianzhi. Li Xianzhi failed to provide evidence proving that the two plots of land belonged to him; therefore, his claim also lacked merit. The Construction Engineering Group requested the court of second instance to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

After the second instance trial, this Court, in addition to confirming the facts found by the first instance court, further found the following facts: In April 1987, the City No.1 Construction Company submitted to the Changchun City Construction Engineering Bureau the "Request of the City No.1 Construction Company Regarding the Trial Implementation of a Shareholding Management System," which stated that, in order to adapt to the needs of economic system reform, further enhance enterprise vitality, and improve economic benefits, the company decided to conduct a pilot project of the shareholding management system at the No.5 Division. The "Provisions on the Trial Implementation of a Shareholding Management System for the No.5 Division" attached to the request stated that, to further reform the enterprise management system, enhance enterprise vitality, and improve economic benefits, the company approved Comrade Li Xianzhi's application to invest equity in the No.5 Division, implement shareholding management, and assume sole responsibility for its profits and losses, and decided to conduct a pilot project of the shareholding management system at that division, specifically as follows: the nature of the enterprise was to be owned by the whole people (state-owned); the enterprise name was the No.5 Division; the shareholding economic composition consisted of an enterprise equity investment accounting for 88% of the total investment amount, contributed by company funds, and individual equity investments accounting for 12% of the investment amount, contributed by the investors; for those investing equity, the policy was voluntary investment, free withdrawal, and asset verification and liquidation... the share price was to be determined on the basis of delineating the ownership of property. After Comrade Li Xianzhi's equity investment, the share price was determined to be 113,600 yuan. The enterprise dividend rate (annual interest) was 8.64%, and the individual dividend rate (annual interest) was 12%. Both types of dividends were to be included in costs. For all equity investors, the company distributed dividends based on the achievement of cost reduction targets, in two tiers: if the planned targets were met, a 20-80 dividend distribution could be implemented; for the portion exceeding the plan, a 40-60 dividend distribution was implemented. Various funds (statutory profits, labor insurance funds, large temporary facility funds, construction profits, technical equipment fees, depreciation funds, and higher-level management fees) were to be paid in full on a monthly basis...

This Court finds, upon trial, that the No.5 Division was an internal independent accounting unit established by the City No.1 Construction Company based on the development needs of the enterprise, with the approval of its supervisory authority, the Construction Engineering Bureau. It did not possess legal person status, was not a civil subject in the legal sense, and had no independent legal person property; all of its property was an indivisible part of the legal person property of the City No.1 Construction Company. As the establishment of an internal department of a legal person, it merely represented an increase in the internal organizational structure of the legal person, different from the formation of a legal person. Therefore, its establishment was not premised on whether property was contributed. Hence, Li Xianzhi's assertion that the City No.1 Construction Company did not contribute any property to the No.5 Division is of no substantial significance in determining the nature of the No.5 Division. Regardless of what type of operational mode was adopted after the establishment of the No.5 Division, or whether Li Xianzhi made contributions to it, none of these could change the legal attribute that the No.5 Division was an internal department of the City No.1 Construction Company.

Judging from the contents of the "Interim Measures on the Implementation of Independent Accounting and Self-Responsibility for Profits and Losses under Contracted Management for the No.5 Division" and the "Provisions on the Trial Implementation of a Shareholding Management System for the No.5 Division" of the City No.1 Construction Company, the City No.1 Construction Company used the No.5 Division as a pilot for its contracted management and shareholding management system. It merely adopted a special mode of operation without thereby changing the attributes of the legal person or the investment structure. Even if, as Li Xianzhi asserts, the City No.1 Construction Company had attempted to adopt a shareholding management mode for the No.5 Division, because the City No.1 Construction Company ultimately did not formally implement a shareholding cooperative system reform — that is, the legal attribute of the City No.1 Construction Company as a state-owned enterprise was not changed, and its investment subjects remained limited to the state, with no other types of investment subjects joining — therefore, although the City No.1 Construction Company's "Provisions on the Trial Implementation of a Shareholding Management System for the No.5 Division" and the 1988 contract used terms such as "individual equity investment" and "invested share amount" with respect to Li Xianzhi's contribution of 125,209 yuan in fixed assets, it is not appropriate to simply conclude on this basis that Li Xianzhi made an individual investment in the City No.1 Construction Company, i.e., Li Xianzhi was not one of the investment subjects of the City No.1 Construction Company. Furthermore, even if it were established that Li Xianzhi made contributions to the City No.1 Construction Company through the shareholding system reform, he could only assert relevant share-related rights and interests against the City No.1 Construction Company as an investor of that company. The No.5 Division would remain an internal department of the City No.1 Construction Company, and all of its property would still be an indivisible part of the legal person property of the City No.1 Construction Company. Therefore, Li Xianzhi's claim that the No.5 Division was established with his personal investment and that all property rights of the No.5 Division belong to him individually, and his request that the Jiangong Group return it, lack factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

Because the No.5 Division was not an independent civil subject, the relationship between Li Xianzhi and the No.5 Division should reflect the legal relationship between Li Xianzhi and the City No.1 Construction Company. Given that the relevant facts involved in this case occurred at the beginning of China's reform and opening up, when enterprise restructuring was still in an exploratory stage, the internal documents of the City No.1 Construction Company — from the 1985 "Report on the Establishment of the No.5 Division" and the "Interim Provisions on the Implementation of Independent Accounting and Self-Responsibility for Profits and Losses under Contracted Management for the No.5 Division," to the 1987 "Provisions on the Trial Implementation of a Shareholding Management System for the No.5 Division," and the 1988 "Notice on the Selection and Appointment of Comrade Zhang Wenshi (including Li Xianzhi) and 59 Other Comrades as Mid-Level Administrative Cadres" — contained different expressions such as contracted management, investment equity, and appointment regarding Li Xianzhi's participation in the operation of the No.5 Division. This confusion and uncertainty were caused by the general social context at that time. Based on the existing evidence, the City No.1 Construction Company and Li Xianzhi did not clearly define the legal relationship between them at the time. The 1988 contract, which both parties recognized, simultaneously contained expressions with different natures such as "contracted management," "investment equity," "dividend (annual interest)," "cost reduction amount," and "dividend distribution." Therefore, it is indeed difficult to accurately define the true legal relationship between the parties at that time using standardized legal concepts more than a decade later. However, this does not affect the accurate definition of the rights and obligations of the contracting parties. According to Article 84 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "obligations are specific rights and obligations arising between parties according to the provisions of a contract or the provisions of law," the 1988 contract signed between Li Xianzhi and the City No.1 Construction Company was a true expression of the parties' intentions, clearly defined their respective rights and obligations, and did not violate laws or administrative regulations. It should serve as the basis for this Court to define the rights and obligations of the parties. Li Xianzhi is entitled to demand that the Jiangong Group perform its obligations in accordance with the contents of the contract. The first instance court, based on the 1988 contract, defined the legal relationship between the two parties as a dual relationship of contracted management and loan. Although this definition may not be entirely accurate in wording, it has positive significance for fairly protecting the rights and interests of all parties. Therefore, this Court upholds that definition. Because when Li Xianzhi participated in the operation of the City No.1 Construction Company, there was no specific legal entity in existence, and the No.5 Division was even less a civil subject established by him individually. Therefore, this Court does not support Li Xianzhi's claim that the No.5 Division was affiliated with the City No.1 Construction Company.

Under the 1988 contract, Li Xianzhi was entitled, on the one hand, to the relevant rights and interests of his 125,209 yuan in fixed assets and an annual fixed return of 15%, and on the other hand, to a 40% dividend distribution on the portion exceeding the cost reduction target of 295,000 yuan after his operation of the No.5 Division. Li Xianzhi is entitled to assert his due benefits from the Jiangong Group. In the first instance court hearing, Li Xianzhi acknowledged that he had received dividends and bonuses totaling 111,837.11 yuan from the City No.1 Construction Company between 1987 and 1992. As to the achievement of the cost reduction target, the only evidence available is the content set forth in the "Audit Report No. 794." However, because that report was an audit conclusion based on partial account books provided by the City No.1 Construction Company, it cannot be used as evidence. In this regard, Li Xianzhi should submit more sufficient evidence to this Court to prove his achievement of the cost reduction target. The "1995 Settlement List," signed and sealed by Li Xianzhi and the Jiangong Group No.1 Construction Company in 1995, clearly showed that after settling the claims and debts between Li Xianzhi and the City No.1 Construction Company (including Li Xianzhi's 125,209 yuan in fund-raising money and unsettled interest), Li Xianzhi still owed the City No.1 Construction Company 107,743.09 yuan. Thereafter, on April 9 of the same year, Li Xianzhi, in the name of another enterprise he had established, Zhixin Company, entered into an "Agreement on Repayment of Debts by Substitution" with the Jiangong Group regarding the 107,743.09 yuan debt owed by Li Xianzhi after settlement. Through this agreement, Zhixin Company actually repaid the 107,743.09 yuan owed by Li Xianzhi after settlement by repaying other debts of the Jiangong Group. The above facts at least indicate that Li Xianzhi acknowledged the debt owed to the Jiangong Group as recorded in the "1995 Settlement List." In the litigation, Li Xianzhi denied that the "1995 Settlement List" represented a full settlement of all his relations with the City No.1 Construction Company from 1985 to 1992, and he bears the burden of proof for this assertion. Since Li Xianzhi has not produced any other evidence to support his claim, the first instance court, based on the settlement result recorded in the "1995 Settlement List," determined that Li Xianzhi and the Jiangong Group had settled all economic transactions between him and the City No.1 Construction Company prior to 1995, and that all of Li Xianzhi's claims against the City No.1 Construction Company had been fully settled. This determination has factual and legal basis, and this Court upholds it. Since Li Xianzhi has already settled his claims and debts with the City No.1 Construction Company through the "1995 Settlement List," this Court will no longer examine the matters of Li Xianzhi's achievement of the cost reduction target, how much dividends and bonuses he should have received from the City No.1 Construction Company, and how much he actually received. As to Li Xianzhi's claim concerning the two plots of land, because Li Xianzhi did not submit evidence to this Court proving his rights to them, this Court also does not support that claim. Li Xianzhi must provide sufficient evidence to this Court for his claims; otherwise, he must bear the legal consequences of failing to meet the burden of proof.

Pursuant to Article 84 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64, Paragraph 1, Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1), and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 110,609 yuan and the audit and appraisal fee of RMB 80,000 yuan, and the second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 110,609 yuan, are all to be borne by Li Ming.

This judgment is final.
